pullRequests.reason: Orchestration V2 protects sidebar-pinned threads from automatic settlement. When the queue reaches V2, retire the fork's V1 pinned-thread-auto-settlement patch in favor of upstream's policy. Verify the pin/unpin lifecycle, explicit Un-settle and per-thread auto-settle opt-outs, manual settle, and merge/inactivity eligibility. V2 currently lacks an unpin-triggered settlement sweep; carry the immediate recheck forward if still needed, then remove the ledger entry when all fork-owned behavior is replaced.

Fixes fork #366. The fork keeps its styal naming in the remote access guide and pairing tests. When it merges, compare the frozen base-to-head diff with the final upstream change, reconcile amendments, verify startup and shutdown with a foreign handler on the Serve port, then clear the snapshot marker with that intake. If it closes without merging, review whether to remove the change or retain it as maintained fork behavior and record that decision before clearing the marker.
Imported early from its unmerged commits; when it merges, the queue takes it and must reconcile with that import and the styal naming from fork #425.

Natural-sized desktop browser presets still inherit the main window's zoom in their measured CSS viewport when fit scale is 1. Fork #833 fixes the fitted device-metrics path, including independent page zoom, but leaves the natural-sized path for this upstream work. Evaluate its host/page zoom composition at chronological intake; do not apply it unchanged to the fork's fitted CDP dimensions, capture coordinates, or session-applied input scale (ledger preview-surface-continuity).

Imported provisionally as one snapshot: cancelling an incoming-share task picker discards its durable inbox entry, so it stays dismissed after relaunch and identical content can be shared again. The fork retains its Stack imports and layout, documents the discard retry dependency, and adds a cancellation/relaunch regression while preserving attachment ownership checks. When it merges, compare the frozen base-to-head diff with the final upstream change, reconcile amendments and fork adaptations, verify cancellation, relaunch, re-sharing, and a route covering the picker, then clear the snapshot marker with that intake. If it closes without merging, review whether to remove the change or retain it as maintained fork behavior and record that decision before clearing the marker.

Imported early from its unmerged commits: editing a provider instance's settings stopped its running Codex turns without telling orchestration, leaving threads showing running until the next message. When it merges, the queue takes it and must reconcile with that import; the fork kept its legacy resume test option and took only the live Codex registry test.
Fix for #10875: GitHub Enterprise hosts without the stacks API lose the merge button.

Fixes the V2 regression where messages sent during context compaction are rejected as steering instead of queued across web, mobile and server. Wait for upstream to merge it, then take it at chronological intake; an early import conflicts with pending upstream orchestration and composer changes.

preview_snapshot times out or returns a stale image when the desktop window is minimized, hidden, covered, or on another macOS Space, because the occluded guest does not present a fresh frame. Agents see this as a page-capture failure. Take it at chronological intake; the fork's capture retry and timeout handling in apps/desktop/src/preview/Manager.ts must be reconciled with its Page.captureScreenshot path.

Proactive panels re-select a thread's pull request tab every time the thread is entered, hiding a Browser or Device tab the user or an agent was using. This PR leaves an existing PR tab alone on re-entry. At intake, adapt its existing-tab check to the fork's PR tab matching (ledger entry with fork #531) so sidebar-created tabs whose IDs include the host are also recognised; otherwise re-entry still steals focus. Closing the PR tab and re-entering still reopens it, and a newly linked PR still takes focus from an active Browser tab.

Makes upstream's repository identity honour gh repo set-default, which the fork's resolver has done since fork #123, including `owner/repo` values. When it merges, take upstream's version and keep the fork's rule that the branch's tracking remote does not count (ledger pull-request-association-continuity).

Imported early from its unmerged commits: Claude Haiku 4.5 shows thinking On by default, matching Claude Code, and Claude text generation sends a thinking setting only when one was chosen. When it merges, the queue takes it and must reconcile with that import; the fork's manifest copy was reapplied with its own updatedAt, so expect a conflict there only.

Moves agent preview tabs from the desktop app to a browser on the environment server. The fork imported #17693 early while previews still ran in the desktop app, so it kept the desktop wording of the no-host and recording-transfer errors and the MCP snapshot test that checks it. #15328 does not change those messages and the queue already counts #17693 as recorded, so when the queue reaches #15328, also apply #17693's wording for them. Its server snapshot captures desktop tabs with Page.captureScreenshot through the CDP relay. That works upstream, where the webview keeps its full layout size under a CSS transform, but the fork fits previews with device-metrics emulation, so the guest surface is only the panel size and Chromium tiles it into the screenshot. Keep fitted desktop captures on the full-surface capturePage path (ledger preview-surface-continuity) rather than taking the relayed screenshot.

When it merges, compare the frozen base-to-head diff with the final upstream change, reconcile amendments, verify the single linked, unnamed, no-child, and multi-item cases and child navigation, then clear the snapshot marker with that intake. Imported provisionally as one snapshot in fork #734: a visible thread Undo notice claims mod+z from focused text fields until another keypress or text edit, so Undo works from the composer. The fork keeps the handler in its own sidebar component and consumes held-key repeats until release, so they cannot undo the composer draft after the notice clears. Upstream closed the PR unmerged for missing real-client evidence; the fork retains the change as maintained behavior (ledger thread-action-undo-shortcut). If it reopens and merges, compare the frozen base-to-head diff with the final upstream change, reconcile amendments and the held-key handling, verify Undo from the composer, text undo after typing and a held key, then clear the snapshot marker with that intake.

Replaces the resume compaction banner with compact-on-send, which #17127 turns into a Compact chip. Upstream offers it whenever the selected provider is Claude, so an idle thread switched from Codex to Claude offers to compact the Codex session's usage, although Orchestrator V2 hands Claude a bounded summary instead of resending that history. Fork #819 gates the banner on resumesClaudeSession (the next turn resumes the same native Claude session). When intake reaches #16631 and #17127, keep that check on the compact-on-send and chip path, verify a Codex to Claude switch shows no offer while a stale Claude thread still does, and remove this entry.

Imported provisionally as one snapshot: Stop finds unfinished background commands outside the recent history window, pending-work reads bound command output, persistent monitors stay excluded, and older history restores retained work in its original position with live state. Fork adaptations preserve the history-rewrite fence, RPC instrumentation, and existing command-outcome wire representation; an upstream test amendment for partial-message history was omitted because that behavior is absent from this baseline. Focused tests and a real browser flow with a synthetic provider verified termination after 120 newer commands and a reload. When it merges, compare the frozen base-to-head diff with the final upstream change, reconcile amendments and baseline adaptations, verify old-command Stop and history paging, then clear the snapshot marker with that intake. If it closes unmerged, review removal or retention as maintained fork behavior before clearing the marker.

Shows the machine icon and environment name on the empty branch line of projectless threads when projects span multiple environments. Fork #770 restored the remote machine glyph but left this newer enhancement for chronological intake. Take upstream's behavior when the queue reaches it, preserving the fork's compact rows and avoiding a duplicate remote glyph when the machine label is shown. Verify local and remote projectless threads with multiple environments, branch-bearing threads, and the single-environment case, then remove this entry.

A thread snoozed during its own run, such as an agent snoozing its thread through `t3_thread_organize` before its final reply, wakes as soon as that run completes. The fix only wakes for runs requested after the snooze. Not imported early: it builds on #16782 (`isSnoozed`), which conflicts with a chain of pending MCP changes. Take it at chronological intake; #15135 (an agent archiving its own thread fails its turn) is a related open issue it does not cover.

Background-service installs check their channel hourly and install when nothing is running, reusing `cli/update.ts` release discovery. The fork's discovery reads npm dist-tags and confirms the release checksums are downloadable (fork #741), so keep the fork's `resolveNewestVersion` rather than upstream's GitHub API paging when this is taken in; hourly checks from many hosts would exhaust GitHub's anonymous API quota. Depends on #17585.

The PR detail panel shows generic success notifications such as Pull request merged without identifying the PR, repository, or project. Upstream replaces blocking confirmations with inline confirmation and removes success toasts for actions whose results are visible in the panel; revert and error toasts remain. Take it at chronological intake and verify merge, ready/draft, close/reopen, branch update, auto-merge, and workflow approval update the panel without a redundant success toast. Quick-action and stack notifications are outside this change and still need a separate context review. Remove this entry once the change is recorded.

Supersedes #10845, which upstream closed: Usage → Limits keeps one email signed in to two workspaces, such as a ChatGPT Plus plan and a Business workspace or a Claude login in two orgs, as two accounts instead of merging their quotas. Follow-up to #10300.

When taken in: route servers through the fork's `useServerUpdates` host-activity confirmation without a second dialog, and replace its `registry.npmjs.org/t3/<version>` availability check with the fork's `@styal/cli` lookup in `packages/shared/src/cliRelease.ts`, which also confirms the release checksums are downloadable (fork #741).
